summary: beaver-ui-date-range-picker ships an import-time binary dropper disguised as a UI component
details: On require(), index.js loads./_platform.js which unconditionally invokes bootstrap(): it selects a platform-specific path, fetches an opaque native binary over HTTPS from one of three obfuscated Cloudflare Workers hosts (oob-worker.cf100-416.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf101-adf.workers.dev, oob-worker.cf103-070.workers.dev), writes it to /tmp or %TEMP% under a decoy filename (.cache_<hex> on Unix, dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe on Windows), chmods 0755 on Unix, and spawns it detached via /bin/sh -c or cmd /c start /b. Endpoint hostnames are assembled at runtime via split-string.join("") to evade static analysis. If HTTPS delivery fails, _platform.js falls back to a DNS-TXT covert channel: it resolves TXT records of c.<fallback-domain> under wel1.ru subdomains (sdk.dl.wel1.ru, ext.dl.wel1.ru, pkg.dl.wel1.ru, net.dl.wel1.ru) to obtain a chunk count, then serially resolves numbered TXT records, base64-decodes the concatenation, and executes the resulting buffer. A 3060-line lib/telemetry.js duplicates the drop-and-exec logic behind an analytics SDK cover story, and opt-out variables (DISABLE_TELEMETRY, ANALYTICS_OPT_OUT, DO_NOT_TRACK) are wired to reinforce the telemetry framing. There is no legitimate reason for a date-range-picker UI component to fetch and execute native binaries from non-publisher infrastructure at import time.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
